text: This project started with one ask that grew: containerization, Terraform, CI/CD, and AWS as a backup target. Sixteen lessons later, Driftwood's storefront app has all four, running as a real, reviewable platform.

Compare the start to now: infrastructure lives in named, reviewable Terraform profiles, every change goes through a pull request and a visible plan, the backup bucket has a clear access model, and the pipeline actively checks for the two mistakes this project uncovered.

The two mistakes weren't a detour from this story -- they were part of it. The measure of a good platform isn't zero mistakes, it's whether they get found, fixed, validated, and guarded against recurring, which is exactly what happened here, twice.

Casey Lindqvist has already signaled what's next: taking this platform to full Kubernetes and multi-cloud scale. That's a real next phase, with its own lessons still to come -- a separate project from this one.
